summary: On March 10, 2024, the City Council passed the Public Safety Enhancement Proposal for downtown by an overwhelming majority, responding to a rise in incidents from petty theft to more serious crimes. The five-part plan covers more officers, surveillance technology, community crime prevention, better lighting, and a public awareness campaign. Business owners and residents spoke in support, funding options including a possible sales tax increase were debated, and City Manager Carlos Reynolds outlined a rollout beginning with recruitment and visible changes by summer.
one_line: City Council passed a five-part downtown public safety plan on March 10, 2024, with rollout starting immediately and visible changes expected by summer.
key_facts: The City Council meeting on public safety took place at City Hall on March 10, 2024.
Downtown had seen a troubling uptick in public safety incidents in recent months, from petty thefts to more severe crimes.
Councilmember James Carter unveiled the proposal, which was developed in response to concerns from businesses and citizens.

The proposal has five elements: more downtown law enforcement officers, surveillance technology (high-definition cameras and emergency assistance kiosks), community-based crime prevention programs, improved street lighting and clear sightlines, and a public awareness campaign.
Amanda Nguyen, a small business owner affected by petty crime, said "We're not only losing revenue; we are losing our customers' trust."
Frank Simmons, head of a local neighborhood watch program, advocated for point three of the proposal on community policing and crime prevention.
Finance Director Emily Moreno presented estimated costs and funding sources: reallocating parts of the city budget, state and federal grants, and potentially a marginal local sales tax increase.
The possible tax increase prompted a spirited exchange among council members; Councilman Richard Lee said "We cannot put a price on our constituents' safety."
The motion passed with an overwhelming majority, announced by Council President Linda Martinez as the Public Safety Enhancement Proposal.
City Manager Carlos Reynolds said implementation begins with immediate recruitment of additional officers and formation of an oversight committee for transparency and community involvement.
Residents can expect enhanced street lighting and increased patrols as early as the beginning of summer 2024.
Reynolds said that by the close of 2024 downtown will be safer and serve as a model for other communities.
